title: Chargino lifetimes, disappearing tracks and the road to a thermal Higgsino: HL-LHC, FCC-hh and a muon collider after LZ
question: Given the LZ-fitting doublet's fixed chargino splitting (P014: 342 MeV, c tau 0.71 cm) and collider-invisible delta ~ 366 keV, what are the quantitative disappearing-track, mono-X and precision-EW reaches of HL-LHC, FCC-hh, a 10 TeV muon collider and FCC-ee/CEPC/ILC, what would each measure, and why is delta unmeasurable at colliders?
headline_result: The LZ-fitting doublet (c tau 0.71 cm) escapes HL-LHC (95% CL reach 300 GeV with 12 cm tracklets, 475 GeV with 5 cm) and is marginal at FCC-hh (95% 1.3-2.05 TeV, 5 sigma at 1.1 TeV), but a 10 TeV muon collider, where beta gamma = 4.4 is fixed and 12.5% of charginos decay beyond 5 cm, gives 1490 tracklets at 1.1 TeV and discovers it to ~3 TeV, measuring m, the multiplet (doublet vs Y=1 triplet at 7.7 sigma) and Delta m+- to 3 MeV; delta is unmeasurable at any collider (chi2 photon 0.06-2 MeV emitted 5e7 m downstream; Delta m+- bounds delta < 4.7-104 GeV), so the inelastic part of the interpretation is direct-detection-only
key_numbers: pairs at 1.1 TeV: HL-LHC 2.3e3, FCC-hh 1.8e6 (sigma_cn 41 fb, /3-x3), MuC 1.7e4 (1.20+0.50 fb; Y=1 triplet 7.81 fb); median beta gamma_T 0.50 (14 TeV) / 0.72 (100 TeV), MuC 4.43; P(r>5 cm) 1.1e-3 / 9.9e-3 / 0.125; eps_kin 0.020 (wino calibration); 95% reach HL-LHC 300/475 GeV (12/5 cm), FCC-hh 1300/2050 GeV (10/5 cm; band 1050-2500), MuC 2100/3350 GeV; 5 sigma FCC-hh 1100/1700, MuC 1900/3150; mono-photon MuC 0.14 fb, S/sqrt(B) 0.22; chi2 photon 63 keV-2.1 MeV (gamma=3), decay length 5e7 m, 0.16 in-detector decays at FCC-hh; delta bound 4.7-104 GeV (10 MeV), 0.7-15 GeV (1.4 MeV); W(1.1 TeV) 1.9e-6, FCC-ee reach 278 GeV; sigma_delta 6.2 keV/sqrt(N) stat, 5% mass -> 0.65 keV
model_or_mechanism: pure Higgsino doublet (and P037 Y=1 triplet); tau-scaled P014 Drell-Yan anchors; tree-level gamma/Z mu+mu- -> chi chi with vector-like chargino coupling; toy pair-mass/angular Drell-Yan model for beta gamma_T; exponential tracklet survival; collinear-ISR mono-photon; chi2 decay kinematics; Delta m+- = Delta m_rad + c_tree delta; oblique W parameter
